published_source: Printed Table 2, Panel A, column (7) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2020.01838.pdf), read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' code output in authors_code_* to the printed decimals. Earlier: Article tables not available in the project (no data/text file). authors_code_* = output of the authors' Replicate.R line 613 on the shipped final data (README: the package reproduces all tables). Table/column labels follow the section comments in Replicate.R (unverified against the article).
replication_status: exact (fixest with the authors' FE reproduces Replicate.R line 613: 0.250623 vs felm 0.250623, SE 0.079500 vs 0.079500, N 432448; article table unavailable)
notes: Kang (2025), 'Price-Fixing Cartels and Firm Innovation', Management Science 71(11). Package: Replicate.R + final cleaned/merged .rds files (real processed data; raw DOJ/VitalLaw, PatentsView and licensed Compustat not shipped). FE: unit + 4-digit-NAICS (patents) or Compustat industry group (R&D) x year (authors: felm(... | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl)); here xt_vars = naics4 (= cl) so the time FE is year + year x cl; SE clustered by cl. No controls, no weights. Outcomes are IHS-transformed counts/amounts, precomputed as ihs_* (log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)), as in Replicate.R). Formation design (primary set): data_reg_patent_from.rds; treated = colluding assignees observed at formation-relative years -4..-1 and +1..+4 (the formation year itself is not in the file; TimeFromYY = year - formation year, verified), post rows all before breakup; controls = all other patenting assignees 1976-2020 (never treated). gvar g_form = formation year (ID_From); D = 1[year >= g_form] equals the authors' TreatY x POST row by row. 3 treated units with pre-sample formation (1975 or earlier) are always-treated in-sample (kept, as in the authors' sample). Unit id uid = assignee_id except for the one assignee in three cartel episodes (226bee8a..., formations 1988/1995/1998 with overlapping windows, the source of all duplicated assignee-years), which is split into three assignee x episode units so that every unit has one adoption date and no duplicated unit-years; this is the only difference from the authors' regression sample and FE.  Pipeline-sample TWFE (raw units) = 0.249851 vs authors 0.250623 (-0.31%).
